title: After 2 nm: will graphene replace silicon? (article and citable PDF)
author: U
text:
Dr. Amir Al Herani
Moderator

I have just published a long article on what the "2 nm" label means physically, and on whether graphene has a realistic route into the logic channel. A short summary for the forum:

1. The node name is a label. In the 2021 IRDS targets for this generation the contacted gate pitch is near 45 nm, the tightest metal pitch is near 20 nm, and the projected physical gate length flattens out around 12 nm. TSMC has not disclosed the physical dimensions of its N2 transistor, but neither its gate length nor its pitch is 2 nm.

2. The limit arrives through electrostatics and tunnelling. I put simple numbers on it: WKB transmission through the source-drain barrier, the natural length λ, and the subthreshold swing.

3. Pristine graphene has no bandgap, which is why large-area graphene FETs commonly showed room-temperature on/off ratios below about ten. The 2024 semiconducting epigraphene result (gap near 0.6 eV, grown on SiC) is important, but it is a long way from 300 mm integration.

4. The two-dimensional material closest to a logic channel is MoS2: a 32-bit RISC-V processor with about 5,900 transistors in 2025, and complementary devices on a 300 mm wafer at a 50 nm contacted poly pitch, reported by imec, ASML and TSMC in June 2026.

5. Graphene's more plausible jobs are outside the digital channel: specialised wiring and optical components of chips that remain predominantly silicon.

My own estimates, which are judgements and not the output of a forecasting model: pristine graphene replacing silicon as the mainstream digital logic channel by 2040, below 5%; a 2D semiconductor such as MoS2 in at least some leading-edge logic-channel applications by 2040, roughly an even chance; silicon still the main substrate for advanced logic manufacturing in 2040, above 95%.
